title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1973-12-01

ai_review.summary: Decent soundboard recording with slight wobble, featuring hot moments like Mexicali Blues and a joyous Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad amid a flat start and fire‑code interruptions.
ai_review.review: The Gardner matrix‑derived soundboard capture is generally clear but shows some width issues, wobble and minor pitch quirks. Musically the concert starts sluggishly, picks up with an uptempo Mexicali Blues, and delivers highlights such as They Love Each Other, Me & My Uncle, a uniquely keyed Uncle John’s Band, and a rousing Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad, though fire‑code pauses disrupt the set flow.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed review points to an average show (flat start, interruptions) with several standout songs, and a decent but not flawless recording; combined weighting yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear Gardner matrix source, slightly better width/hall than pure soundboard, minor wobble and pitch correction needed; other sources suffer wow & flutter.

standout_songs: Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad
poor_songs: Early warm‑up songs (first few of set 1)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts flat and warms up by Mexicali Blues, then drifts into below‑average material; second set is broken up by fire‑code interruptions and banter but recovers with strong performances.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia races through the early songs, fires everyone on Uncle John's Band with a different key/diatonic scale, delivering high energy throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir backs into the hot‑rod feel and adds vocal character (bottle/jaw) though lyric recall is fuzzy at times.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboards contribute to the hot rod momentum, especially on early uptempo numbers.
